title: Distributed Systems Fundamentals
description: Understand CAP theorem, consistency models, distributed transactions, and the fundamentals of building reliable distributed systems.

data.text: The CAP theorem states that a distributed system can only provide two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. Understanding this tradeoff is fundamental to distributed system design.

data.title: Partition Tolerance is Mandatory
data.text: In distributed systems, network partitions are inevitable. Therefore, you must choose between CP (consistency over availability) or AP (availability over consistency). CA is not possible in true distributed systems.

Different consistency models offer different tradeoffs between consistency and availability. Strong consistency ensures all nodes see the same data simultaneously, while eventual consistency allows temporary divergence.

data.text: Two-phase commit (2PC) provides ACID transactions across distributed services but has significant performance and availability costs. The saga pattern provides eventual consistency with better availability.

data.title: Saga Pattern Implementation
Key Takeaways
points: CAP theorem: Choose between CP (consistency) or AP (availability) when partitions occur
Strong consistency is simpler but less available; eventual consistency is more available but more complex
Two-phase commit provides ACID but has poor availability and performance
Saga pattern provides eventual consistency with better availability and scalability
Compensating transactions are essential for saga rollback
Choose consistency model based on business requirements, not technical preference
data.takeaway: Distributed systems require different thinking than monolithic applications. Understand CAP theorem, choose appropriate consistency models, and use patterns like saga to handle distributed transactions.
